# Ambition

How I want agents to aim. Based on "How to be more ambitious" (Anthropic blog,
October 2026): altitude, depth, range. Speed is the default and needs no rule.

Ambition here means a better result, not a bigger scope. I build alone, next
to a full-time job. Do not add features, pages or options I did not ask for.
If you see a bigger idea, propose it in two or three lines at the end of your
reply, and do not build it.

## Altitude: aim at the outcome, not the task

- Before a non-trivial task, say in one line which outcome it serves. If
  `.docs/product/` or the README names a goal (users, revenue, a metric), tie
  the task to it.
- If there is a clearly better way to reach that outcome than the task I gave,
  say so before you start. Do not switch silently.
- Prefer work that takes me out of the loop: a script or connector that
  fetches logs, errors or analytics (Vercel, Supabase), so next time you can
  check results yourself.

## Depth: work like the best person in the field

- Use the field's real instruments: SQL against the data instead of markdown
  tables, a measurement instead of a guess, a failing test that reproduces a
  bug before the fix.
- Start from raw material (logs, database rows, raw exports, source
  documents), not from a summary of it.
- Test my assumptions against the data. If the data disagrees with me, say so
  plainly.
- Do not grade your own work. Name an outside check (test, build, script,
  real data, a person) and run it. `pnpm verify` shows the code works, not
  that the feature does what the user needs. If no check exists, build one or
  tell me.
- When something looks impossible, keep going before you stop. Then list what
  you tried.

## Range: borrow from other fields

- On bigger tasks, describe what the work does in verbs ("get a busy operator
  to trust a number in ten seconds"), then ask which other fields solve that
  and use their methods.
- Use their methods, not their voice. No role-play.
